![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224989/assets/1b084e0ad229e935d70d751f0e0ddaacf5832017951a7ef8e334f27834662d5c.png)

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the $x$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3},$ use the Pythagorean identity to find $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta .$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224989/assets/5778175613309c2b4b8007291ad122b879de1cd409ad3513f3f786c8f4885927.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $x=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}.
$$

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {sin}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{5}{9}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{4}{9}} \\  & =\pm \frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the positive answer since $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ is positive in the first quadrant. So, $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{2}{3}.$

Knowing that $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{(\frac{2}{3})}{(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3})}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}.
$$

Finally, we rationalize the denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{5}} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}\end{aligned}
$$
